question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 36
Article 37
Article 38
Article 39
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 37

Explanation:
In the Part IV of the Indian Constitution, Articles 36 to 51 contain the Directive Principles of State Policy. Article 37 explicitly states that these principles are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country and shall be applied in making laws. This article makes the Directive Principles non-justiciable, meaning no legal action can be taken in court for their violation. They serve as guidelines for the state to establish social and economic justice.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद कहता है कि निर्देशक सिद्धांत किसी भी न्यायालय द्वारा लागू करने योग्य नहीं हैं? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में अनुच्छेद 36 से 51 तक निर्देशक सिद्धांत दिए गए हैं। अनुच्छेद 37 स्पष्ट रूप से कहता है कि ये सिद्धांत किसी न्यायालय द्वारा लागू करने योग्य नहीं हैं, लेकिन ये देश के शासन में मौलिक हैं और विधि निर्माण में इन्हें लागू किया जाना चाहिए। यह अनुच्छेद निर्देशक सिद्धांतों को गैर-न्यायिक बनाता है, अर्थात इनके उल्लंघन पर न्यायालय में याचिका दायर नहीं की जा सकती। ये सिद्धांत नीति-निर्देशक हैं और राज्य को सामाजिक एवं आर्थिक न्याय स्थापित करने में मार्गदर्शन करते हैं।

question: According to Article 335 of the Constitution of India, claims of SCs and STs shall be taken into consideration in matters of: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: taxation policies
religious freedom
land acquisition
public employment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is public employment

Explanation:
Article 335 of the Constitution mandates that claims of SCs and STs shall be taken into consideration in matters of public employment, while maintaining administrative efficiency. This provision is crucial for ensuring social justice and forms the legal basis for reservation in government jobs. Read with Article 16(4), it upholds the principle of equality while addressing historical inequalities. The 77th Amendment (2000) clarified that promotions for SCs/STs are also covered under Article 335. It balances the right to equality under Article 16 with the need for social upliftment. This ensures that weaker sections get adequate representation in public services without compromising efficiency.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the main subject of Article 335? → Consideration of claims of SCs/STs in public employment
☛ Why does Article 335 mention 'administrative efficiency'? → To balance reservation with efficiency
☛ Which amendment included promotions under Article 335? → 77th Amendment (2000)
☛ Article 335 is related to which fundamental right? → Article 16 (Right to Equality)
☛ Does Article 335 provide absolute right to reservation? → No, it is subject to conditions
question_hi: भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 335 के अनुसार, SC और ST के दावों पर किन मामलों में विचार किया जाएगा: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)

धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सार्वजनिक रोजगार

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 335 के अनुसार, सरकारी नौकरियों में एससी और एसटी के दावों पर विचार किया जाना चाहिए, बशर्ते प्रशासन की दक्षता बनी रहे। यह संविधान का एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रावधान है जो सामाजिक न्याय सुनिश्चित करता है। अनुच्छेद 16(4) के साथ पढ़ा जाने वाला यह अनुच्छेद आरक्षण का कानूनी आधार प्रदान करता है। 2000 के संवैधानिक संशोधन ने इसमें यह स्पष्ट किया कि अनुच्छेद 335 के तहत एससी/एसटी के लिए आरक्षण में पदोन्नति भी शामिल है। यह प्रावधान समानता के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 16) और सामाजिक न्याय के बीच संतुलन स्थापित करता है।

question: Which Fundamental Right guarantees Freedom of Speech, Assembly and Movement? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Right to Cultural Rights
Right to Equality
Right to Freedom
Right to Constitutional Remedies
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Freedom

Explanation:
Under Article 19 of the Indian Constitution, the Right to Freedom grants citizens six freedoms, including Freedom of Speech and Expression, Freedom to Assemble Peaceably, and Freedom of Movement. This right is part of Part III of the Constitution. Article 19(1)(a) deals with freedom of speech, 19(1)(b) with assembly, and 19(1)(d) with movement. This fundamental right ensures personal development and democratic participation. However, these freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions. The Right to Equality (Articles 14-18) protects against discrimination. Cultural Rights protect minority interests. The Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) is a means to enforce other rights.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article guarantees Freedom of Speech? → Article 19(1)(a)
☛ Which article guarantees Freedom of Assembly? → Article 19(1)(b)
☛ Which article guarantees Freedom of Movement? → Article 19(1)(d)
☛ Which articles impose restrictions on Right to Freedom? → Articles 19(2) to 19(6)
☛ Which article provides Right to Constitutional Remedies? → Article 32
question_hi: कौन सा मौलिक अधिकार भाषण, सभा और आंदोलन की स्वतंत्रता की गारंटी देता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: सांस्कृतिक अधिकारों का अधिकार
समानता का अधिकार
स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार
संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 19 के तहत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार नागरिकों को छह स्वतंत्रताएं प्रदान करता है, जिनमें भाषण और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता, शांतिपूर्वक सभा करने की स्वतंत्रता और आंदोलन की स्वतंत्रता शामिल हैं। यह अधिकार संविधान के भाग III में शामिल है। अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) भाषण की स्वतंत्रता, 19(1)(b) सभा की स्वतंत्रता, और 19(1)(d) आंदोलन की स्वतंत्रता से संबंधित है। यह मौलिक अधिकार नागरिकों को व्यक्तिगत विकास और लोकतांत्रिक भागीदारी सुनिश्चित करता है। हालाँकि, ये स्वतंत्रताएं उचित प्रतिबंधों के अधीन हैं। समानता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14-18) भेदभाव से सुरक्षा देता है। सांस्कृतिक अधिकार अल्पसंख्यकों के हितों की रक्षा करते हैं। संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 32) अन्य अधिकारों को लागू करने का माध्यम है।

question: Which of the following is NOT a function under the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Public health
Foreign trade promotion
Urban poverty alleviation
Urban planning
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Foreign trade promotion

Explanation:
The Twelfth Schedule was added by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992. It lists 18 functions of Municipalities. Urban planning, urban poverty alleviation, and public health are included in this schedule. Foreign trade promotion is a subject of the central government, falling under the Union List (List I), not the Twelfth Schedule. This function is handled by the Ministry of Commerce, not by municipal bodies. Hence, it is NOT a function under the Twelfth Schedule.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ How many functions are in the Twelfth Schedule? → 18
☛ Where is urban planning listed? → Twelfth Schedule
☛ Which list does foreign trade belong to? → Union List
☛ Is public health in the Twelfth Schedule? → Yes

शहरी नियोजन

Solution: सही उत्तर है विदेशी व्यापार संवर्धन

Explanation:
बारहवीं अनुसूची 74वें संविधान संशोधन, 1992 द्वारा जोड़ी गई। इसमें नगर पालिकाओं के 18 कार्य सूचीबद्ध हैं। शहरी नियोजन, शहरी गरीबी उन्मूलन और सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य इस अनुसूची के अंतर्गत आते हैं। विदेशी व्यापार संवर्धन केंद्र सरकार का विषय है, जो संघ सूची (List I) में आता है, न कि बारहवीं अनुसूची में। यह कार्य वाणिज्य मंत्रालय द्वारा किया जाता है, नगर निकायों द्वारा नहीं। अतः यह बारहवीं अनुसूची का कार्य नहीं है।

question: The Inter-State Council is constituted under which Article? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 263
Article 368
Article 280
Article 346
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 263

Explanation:
The Inter-State Council is constituted under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution. This council is formed to coordinate between the Centre and States and to investigate and advise on disputes arising between them. The President has the authority to establish such a council in the public interest. The Sarkaria Commission recommended the formation of this council. Article 368 deals with Constitutional Amendment, Article 280 deals with Finance Commission, and Article 346 deals with Official Language.

question: Which non-constitutional body investigates corruption complaints against public servants?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Finance Commission
Lokpal
Election Commission
Union Public Service Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lokpal

Explanation:
Lokpal is a non-constitutional body established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 to investigate corruption complaints against public servants of the central government, including the Prime Minister, Ministers, and MPs. It is a statutory body created to combat corruption. In contrast, the Finance Commission, Election Commission, and Union Public Service Commission are constitutional bodies established under the Constitution of India. The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and up to eight members, with the Chairperson appointed through a process similar to that of the Chief Justice of India.

☛ When was Lokpal formed? → 2013
☛ How is the Chairperson of Lokpal appointed? → Similar to the appointment of the Chief Justice of India

question: According to constitutional provisions, what is the maximum permissible size of a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: 20% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
No specific limit is defined
15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
10% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly

Explanation:
According to Article 164(1A) of the Indian Constitution, the total number of ministers in a state's Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that state. This provision was added by the 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) to curb the increasing size of state cabinets. Its aim was to impose financial discipline and ensure efficient governance. This rule applies to all states, irrespective of the size of their assembly. The limit includes the Chief Minister, but every state must have at least 12 ministers in the council. This provision balances representation and administrative efficiency. It prevents bloated cabinets and ensures that the government remains accountable and manageable. The amendment was a key reform to strengthen democratic governance in states.

☛ Percentage limit → 15% of total assembly members

question: What is the correct order of the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure from bottom to top in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Panchayat Samiti – Gram Panchayat – Zila Parishad
Gram Sabha – Gram Panchayat – Zila Parishad
Gram Panchayat – Panchayat Samiti – Zila Parishad
Zila Parishad – Panchayat Samiti – Gram Panchayat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gram Panchayat – Panchayat Samiti – Zila Parishad

Explanation:
The Panchayati Raj system in India is a three-tier structure functioning from village to district level. At the lowest level is the Gram Panchayat, which is elected by the Gram Sabha and looks after village development. Above it is the Panchayat Samiti (block level), which coordinates several Gram Panchayats. The topmost tier is the Zila Parishad (district level), which oversees planning and development of the entire district. This structure was given constitutional status by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992.

question: Which Amendment of the Citizenship Act introduced the provision that an illegal migrant cannot acquire citizenship by naturalisation or registration?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: 2015 Amendment
1986 Amendment
2005 Amendment
2003 Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2003 Amendment

Explanation:
The Citizenship Act of 1955 was amended in 2003, which is one of the most significant amendments. It introduced the definition of 'illegal migrant' for the first time and stipulated that such a person cannot acquire citizenship by naturalisation or registration. According to this amendment, an illegal migrant is a person who enters India without valid documents or stays beyond the permitted period. The 2003 Amendment also introduced the concept of dual citizenship, later replaced by the Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) scheme. This amendment is distinct from the 1986, 1992, and 2005 amendments because it includes strict provisions against illegal migrants. Thus, the 2003 Amendment prevents illegal migrants from obtaining citizenship.

question: Which Act first recognised the political and administrative functions of the East India Company in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which state has special constitutional provisions to protect its tribal customs and laws under Article 371A? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)

Under this article, any law passed by the Parliament applies to Nagaland only if the state's Legislative Assembly passes a resolution to that effect. question: Which of the following Constitutional provisions can be amended by an ordinary Act of Parliament (simple majority), rather than through the special procedure under Article 368? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 2 (Parliament may by law admit new states)
Article 356 (President’s Rule in states)
Article 368 (the Amendment procedure itself)
Article 14 (equality before law)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 2 (Parliament may by law admit new states)

Explanation:
Certain provisions of the Indian Constitution can be amended by an ordinary Act of Parliament passed by a simple majority, rather than through the special procedure under Article 368. Article 2 empowers Parliament to admit or establish new states by a simple legislative act. Such provisions include Article 3 (alteration of state boundaries), Article 4 (amendments to the First and Fourth Schedules), Article 169 (abolition or creation of Legislative Councils), and Article 239A (creation of local legislatures for Union Territories). These provisions are not part of the Constitution's basic structure, so they require only a simple majority. In contrast, Article 356 and Article 368 require special majorities, and Article 14 is a fundamental right that can only be amended under Article 368.

question: Which of the following options correctly describes the scope of judicial review under the Constitution of India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)

Judicial review is explicitly mentioned in the Constitution (Article 13).
Both, Supreme Court and High Courts can strike down unconstitutional laws.
Courts can review any law only after approval by the Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both, Supreme Court and High Courts can strike down unconstitutional laws.

Explanation:
Under the Constitution of India, the power of judicial review is vested in both the Supreme Court and the High Courts. Article 13 directs that all laws in force at the commencement of the Constitution and future laws must conform to Fundamental Rights. Although the term 'judicial review' is not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution, it is an essential part of the basic structure. The Supreme Court can strike down any unconstitutional law, while High Courts can declare laws unconstitutional within their territorial jurisdiction. This power ensures that the legislature and executive do not exceed their constitutional limits. Thus, the correct option is Option 3.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that a person who had voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign State shall NOT be considered a citizen of India at the commencement of the Constitution under Articles 5, 6, or 8? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which special representation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies was discontinued by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2020?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Reservation for Women
SC/ST Reservation
Anglo-Indian Reservation
OBC Reservation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Anglo-Indian Reservation

Explanation:
The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2020 discontinued the reservation of seats for the Anglo-Indian community in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. This reservation was originally provided under Article 331 for the Lok Sabha, allowing the President to nominate two Anglo-Indian members, and under Article 333 for State Assemblies, allowing the Governor to nominate members. The amendment came into effect on 25 January 2020. While it extended the reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes until 2030, it completely removed the Anglo-Indian reservation, marking the end of a special representation that had been in place since the Constitution's adoption.

question: Which of the following constitutional mechanisms ensures political representation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Indian Parliament? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 15 and 16
Article 341 and 342
Article 330 and 332
Article 338 and 339
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 330 and 332

Explanation:
Article 330 and 332 of the Indian Constitution provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies respectively. This is the constitutional mechanism ensuring political representation. Articles 15 and 16 deal with social equality and equal opportunity in public employment. Articles 341 and 342 define the lists of SCs and STs. Articles 338 and 339 establish the National Commission for SCs and the National Commission for STs. Thus, for parliamentary representation, Articles 330 and 332 are correct.

question: Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1953 by separating Telugu-speaking areas from which of the following states?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Madras
Kerala
Karnataka
Tamil Nadu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Madras

Explanation:
Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 October 1953 by separating the Telugu-speaking areas from the Madras State. It became the first state in India to be formed on a linguistic basis. The movement for a separate state was led by Potti Sriramulu, who undertook a fast unto death and died on 15 December 1952. His sacrifice compelled Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru to announce the formation of linguistic states. The Madras State later became the present-day Tamil Nadu. Subsequently, in 1956, the States Reorganisation Commission merged the Telangana region with Andhra Pradesh to form the enlarged state.

question: Which Fundamental Right was removed from the Indian Constitution by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Right to Property
Right to Freedom
Right to Education
Right to Equality
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Property

Explanation:
The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution. It was downgraded to a legal right under Article 300A. This amendment was enacted by the Morarji Desai government to balance individual property rights with the needs of land reforms and social welfare. Now, no person can be deprived of their property except by authority of law. The removal aimed to reduce litigation and support equitable distribution of resources.

question: Which of the following statements about the Right to Property in India is correct?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: It is a fundamental right under Article 31 (now omitted)
It was completely abolished by the Forty-Second Amendment (1976).
It is a fundamental right under Article 32 of the Constitution.
It is no longer a fundamental right.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is no longer a fundamental right

Explanation:
The Right to Property was originally a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 of the Indian Constitution. The 44th Amendment (1978) removed it from the list of fundamental rights and made it a constitutional right under Article 300A. This amendment came into effect in 1979. The 42nd Amendment (1976) did not abolish the right to property; it only expanded the scope of Article 31C. Currently, no person can be deprived of property except by authority of law. It is no longer a fundamental right but a legal/constitutional right.

question: Which of the following subjects is addressed by the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Panchayati Raj system
Emergency powers and procedures
Official languages
Provisions related to anti-defection
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Provisions related to anti-defection

Explanation:
The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with anti-defection provisions. It was added by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985. The main objective is to prevent elected members from switching parties arbitrarily, thereby ensuring political stability. According to the Schedule, a member can be disqualified if they voluntarily give up party membership or vote against party directions. The Presiding Officer of the House (Speaker/Chairman) has the final authority to decide disqualification cases. In the landmark Kihoto Hollohan case (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that the Speaker's decision under the Tenth Schedule is subject to judicial review. The Schedule aims to curb the practice of defection, which was destabilizing governments.

☛ What is the purpose of anti-defection law? → Maintain political stability
☛ Who decides on defection cases? → Presiding Officer of the House
☛ Which case related to Tenth Schedule? → Kihoto Hollohan case (1992)
☛ What constitutes defection? → Voluntary resignation or voting against party
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान की दसवीं अनुसूची निम्नलिखित में से किस विषय को संबोधित करती है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है दल-बदल विरोधी प्रावधान

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की दसवीं अनुसूची दल-बदल विरोधी प्रावधानों से संबंधित है। इसे 1985 में 52वें संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। इसका उद्देश्य निर्वाचित सदस्यों को एक पार्टी से दूसरी में जाने से रोकना है, जिससे राजनीतिक स्थिरता बनी रहे। अनुसूची के अनुसार, यदि कोई सदस्य स्वेच्छा से अपनी पार्टी की सदस्यता छोड़ता है या पार्टी के निर्देशों के विरुद्ध मतदान करता है, तो वह सदन की सदस्यता खो सकता है। इस अनुसूची के तहत अंतिम निर्णय लेने का अधिकार सदन के अध्यक्ष या स्पीकर को होता है। 1992 में किहोतो हॉलोहन मामले में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने फैसला सुनाया कि इस अनुसूची के तहत स्पीकर के फैसले की न्यायिक समीक्षा संभव है।
